title: Scalar-Tensor Hydrodynamics: Gravity as the Response of a Vacuum Medium. A Modified Gravity Framework for Vacuum Viscosity and Cyclic Vacuum Cosmology
description:
A theoretical proposal built on one premise: there is no empty space. The vacuum is treated as a single continuous medium, the Ocean, with its own stress-energy, pressure and internal flow, and with no edges and no outside. What are conventionally called particles are treated as localized excitations of the medium, and gravity is proposed to be the medium's response to concentrated energy. The medium has one speed, at which every disturbance travels. No speed is fixed: the measured speed of light is the local carrying speed read by rulers and clocks made of the same medium. Einstein's equation is retained as the effective description of that response.

The paper sets out the framework's equations and what follows from them: General Relativity's geometry outside resting and spinning masses, and the frame dragging measured by Gravity Probe B and the LAGEOS and LARES satellites; a first-order law that one speed and the preservation of energy and momentum fix uniquely; a continuous rebuild of every pattern, in which gravity is the uneven making of time; an eddy in the medium's flow that gives galaxies their extra turning with one acceleration scale; the medium's grip, which stops a collapse and turns it; and a cyclic cosmology, in which a beat's end becomes the next beat's beginning.

What would end the framework as written is listed first among the open items, each with what is open, what settles it and what would make it fail; the predictions are gathered in a section of their own, each with its test. Every part of the paper carries a checksum token, and a reading manifest with a document digest lets any reader confirm a complete reading. What each version changed is recorded in the paper's preface and in the release notes at github.com/hunanguy/Ocean.

Version 3.16 tests the framework against measurement and stops using numbers fitted by the standard account. Between beats the Ocean is first a gas of light and then a normal fluid, which the first builds make into the Ocean nearly all at once; the microwave background is the light of those builds' pairs. The eddy now answers at each place to the galaxy's own turning there. Fitted to 153 galaxies one by one with one limit for all, it does nearly as well as the measured radial acceleration relation; fitted to the real Milky Way's rotation curve and the up-and-down motions of stars near the Sun, it does as well as a halo of cold dark matter, on the test that ruled out superfluid dark matter. The settled Ocean's slow thinning, fitted to DESI's galaxy distances and three sets of supernovae, does about as well as DESI's own formula, with one number fewer and without dark energy growing denser in the past. The Hubble constant comes only from its direct measurements. The analyses, their data and the fits are in the repository's sparc, milky-way and expansion folders. Document digest 8563-1f7b-50ca.

This is a proposal, not an established theory. The document states its own falsification conditions explicitly and carries an itemized research program, several items of which could terminate the framework.
notes: Built reproducibly from build_ocean_formalism.py; requires pdflatex. Document digest 8563-1f7b-50ca. Appendix A is also issued as a standalone PDF. The analyses behind Sections 5.1 and 6 are in the repository's sparc, milky-way and expansion folders.
